The second counted item is the pull request #5, which carries both labels but is never listed by the link, so the number and its list can never agree.

findings.name: Assigning a label that was deleted meanwhile fails with a 500 and is silently ignored
findings.summary: The label gets a check mark as if assigned, and nothing tells the user anything is wrong. When the picker is closed the request POST /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/labels fails with 500 Internal Server Error, the check mark is gone, the sidebar still shows only "documentation" and no error message is displayed anywhere. The stale deleted label also remains in the picker's list until the page is reloaded. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/7 (sidebar label picker))
findings.expected: The app tells the user the label could not be applied (it no longer exists) instead of failing silently with a 500 server error, and the deleted label does not stay listed as assignable.
findings.actual: The label gets a check mark as if assigned, and nothing tells the user anything is wrong. When the picker is closed the request POST /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/labels fails with 500 Internal Server Error, the check mark is gone, the sidebar still shows only "documentation" and no error message is displayed anywhere. The stale deleted label also remains in the picker's list until the page is reloaded.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1.
On /eval/harbor-handbook/labels create a label named 'agent11-vanish' (description 'Agent11 delete while picker open test', colour #ff8800) and Save.
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/7 (issue 'agent11-dialog-fixture') and open the label picker from the 'Labels' row of the right sidebar — 'agent11-vanish' is listed.
In a second browser tab open /eval/harbor-handbook/labels and delete the label 'agent11-vanish' (Delete → Confirm, page says 'The label has been deleted.').
Back in the first tab, click 'agent11-vanish' in the still-open picker — a check mark appears next to it as if the label had been assigned.
Click somewhere else on the issue page to close the picker.

(on /eval/harbor-handbook/labels?sort=leastissues&state=)
findings.expected: Under "Least issues" the labels are ordered by the number shown next to them, smallest first, so a label with "1 open issues/pull requests" always comes before a label with "2 open issues/pull requests".
findings.actual: The list is not in ascending order of the numbers shown: the tail reads agent14-tablet-label "1 open issues/pull requests", documentation "2 open issues/pull requests", then agent7-count "1 open issues/pull requests", then enhancement. The label with 1 open item is listed after the label with 2. After removing the label from closed issue #3 (leaving agent7-count with only its 1 open issue), the same sort put agent7-count correctly before documentation, so the order follows a count that includes closed issues, while the number on the page counts only open ones.

Open open issue #2 (https://5503-ihto2i2dj1c31tlfb1unv.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/issues/2), click "Labels" in the right sidebar, pick "agent7-count", then click anywhere outside the picker so it saves

findings.name: Alt+Enter in the Label filter excludes nothing: it applies a normal include filter for the label
findings.summary: Alt+Enter behaves as a plain include: the page ends on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues?type=all&state=open&labels=2 (label 2 = enhancement) and the list shows only the 3 issues that HAVE enhancement (#8, #6, #4) out of 9 open issues — the opposite of excluding them. A request to ?labels=-2 is fired first and aborted, then the include filter is applied; the dropdown gives no excluded state at all. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues)
findings.expected: Alt+Enter on a label in the Label filter excludes that label: the list shows the 6 issues that do NOT have 'enhancement', the chosen label is visibly marked as excluded and can be removed again.
findings.actual: Alt+Enter behaves as a plain include: the page ends on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues?type=all&state=open&labels=2 (label 2 = enhancement) and the list shows only the 3 issues that HAVE enhancement (#8, #6, #4) out of 9 open issues — the opposite of excluding them. A request to ?labels=-2 is fired first and aborted, then the include filter is applied; the dropdown gives no excluded state at all.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues (9 open issues, 3 of them have the label 'enhancement')
Click the 'Label' filter button in the toolbar so its dropdown opens, and note the hint 'Use alt + click/enter to exclude labels'
Type 'enhancement' into the dropdown's filter box, press ArrowDown to highlight the 'enhancement' option, then press Alt+Enter
Read the address bar and the resulting list and the Open/Closed counters
